exposure: Ratio of resting levator hiatus diameter (LHS) to fetal head circumference (HC) at 37 weeks of gestation
outcome: Progression of the second stage of labor (duration > 1 hour)
cohort: The study included 120 primiparous women who delivered vaginally at 37 weeks of pregnancy.
finding: The ratio of resting levator hiatus diameter (LHS) to fetal head circumference (HC) showed the highest predictive value for both prolongation of the second stage of labor and postpartum levator ani muscle injury.
mod_finding: Early detection of the ratio of resting LHS and fetal HC is helpful to guide the selection of an appropriate delivery mode.
